clue.text: VIPs sent back prize money

indicators.note: something sent back goes the way it came, so the word for prize is read from its end

blocks.note: a pot is a prize or jackpot
brass is informal British slang for money

explanation.surface: Important people return the prize money they were awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Top brass is an idiom for the highest-ranking officers or officials, the very important people of an organisation.

clue.text: Predictable? In part, yes?

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about whether something can be foreseen
setter's reading: an actor always given the same kind of role is predictable in the part they play

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing is predictable and half concedes that it partly is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' is a stage role, not a portion: an actor who is always cast as the same type is predictable in every part.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor typecast in the same role over and over gives performances an audience can foresee, hence predictable.

clue.text: Song prize split by son

indicators.note: a word split by another is broken open with the other placed in the gap

blocks.note: the palm is a symbol of victory, hence a prize
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A prize-winning song is shared with someone's son.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Courtier and a girl he aroused

indicators.note: something aroused is stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A courtier and a girl he has excited: a hint of romance at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh was a famous courtier and favourite of Queen Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Crack on sale by river vexes some upper-class young ladies

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for river
to vex someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Cheap drugs sold beside a river annoy a set of posh young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like the drug, but it is the anagram signal. Sloane Rangers, named after Sloane Square in London's wealthy Chelsea, were a 1980s label for fashionable upper-class young people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a British social label for well-off, upper-class young women living in fashionable west London.

clue.text: Slang for a variety of zircon

blocks.note: first meaning: specialised or obscure language of a group
second meaning: a colourless or smoky form of the gemstone zircon

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the slang term is for a particular kind of zircon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a group's specialised terminology and also, as a mineral name, a pale or smoky zircon gemstone.

clue.text: A small country in an ancient kingdom

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Syria is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A little country lies within the borders of an old kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the modern country sits in the region the old kingdom once ruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was a major kingdom of ancient Mesopotamia, centred on the upper Tigris.

clue.text: Piece about one girl about to become a legendary paramour

indicators.note: one thing about another goes round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a piece is slang for a firearm
I is the Roman numeral one
Eve is a girl's name
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A story about a girl who is set to become a famous lover of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'about' wraps the gun round the one; the second 'about' is itself a piece of the answer. 'Piece' means a firearm here, not a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend Guinevere, King Arthur's queen, was the lover of the knight Lancelot.

clue.text: Joe perhaps, quite an age

definitions.note: the number in a title, standing for its bearer

blocks.note: first meaning: Joe 90 was a 1960s British puppet TV series by Gerry Anderson
second meaning: a very old age for a person to reach

explanation.surface: Remarking that old Joe has lived to a great age.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe 90 was a British children's puppet series about a nine-year-old secret agent, so Joe is tagged with the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching nine decades is a notably long life, and the number also completes the puppet hero's title.

clue.text: Girl, pretty small type

blocks.note: first meaning: a girl's name
second meaning: an old printers' name for a very small type size, about five points

explanation.surface: A girl described as pretty and petite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a kind of person, but it is a printing font size.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name and also a traditional printing term for a tiny typeface size.

clue.text: Preoccupation of old boy before meeting

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a session is a meeting or sitting

explanation.surface: A former pupil is anxious ahead of a reunion meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a fixation that occupies the mind continually, a synonym for preoccupation.

clue.text: Drug dealer, one not hanging about?

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a merchant is a dealer or trader

explanation.surface: A pusher is someone who never loiters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' reads as one phrase, but splits into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed merchant is informal for someone who goes very fast, so certainly not one to dawdle or linger.

clue.text: Film director affected one acting

blocks.note: camp means exaggerated or affected in manner
I is the Roman numeral one
an actor on stage is on, performing

explanation.surface: A movie director influenced someone who performs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like a verb (influenced), but it is the adjective meaning mannered.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Campion is the New Zealand film director of The Piano and The Power of the Dog.

clue.text: Seriousness shown by boy hugging adult

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: Ernest is a boy's name
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A boy embracing a grown-up shows how serious he is.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest wraps around the adult's single letter, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest as a noun means seriousness, as in the phrase 'in earnest'.

clue.text: Chess ending overwhelmed friend

blocks.note: to be smothered is to be overwhelmed
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A chess game ends with one's friend crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A smothered mate is a checkmate by a knight on a king hemmed in by its own pieces, ending the game.

clue.text: Sold roués bubbly without a distinctive smell

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and churning, so these letters are churned into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rakes were sold champagne that had no particular bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne, the noun, but works as the anagram signal. A roué is a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: Odourless means having no scent at all, so lacking any distinctive smell.

clue.text: Hit man, for instance, on cheek, at home

blocks.note: as introduces an example, as in 'such as'
sass is impudence, or cheek
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A contract killer, for example, gets slapped in the face while at home.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer of a prominent person, which a hit man is in slang.

clue.text: Train - direct, say

blocks.note: to orient something is to direct or position it
to express is to say or put into words

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer a train and tell it what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient Express is the famous luxury long-distance train linking Paris and Istanbul.

clue.text: In pursuance of an investigation

blocks.note: taken as written
a quest is a pursuit or search

explanation.surface: Pursuing an inquiry, in formal official language.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquest is a judicial investigation, typically by a coroner into a death.

clue.text: Bother a tennis star after end of championship

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
taken as written
Rod Laver, the Australian who twice won tennis's Grand Slam

explanation.surface: A tennis star is bothered once the championship is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the star after the final letter of the championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is informal for fuss or trouble, so a bother or hassle.

clue.text: Heart and clubs put down, reportedly

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the answer is what the pieces sound like

blocks.note: C is clubs in card notation; to enter is to put down or record

explanation.surface: Someone at cards lays down hearts and clubs, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart and clubs are card suits on the surface, but only clubs is wordplay; heart is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its middle or core, a synonym for centre.

clue.text: Spanish boy in queer comic

indicators.note: something comic is funny or absurd, so these letters are put into a silly new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish lad appears in an odd comic book.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrique is a common Spanish male first name, the equivalent of Henry.

clue.text: Short girl on a keyboard instrument

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the name loses its final letter

blocks.note: Celeste is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A short girl sits at a keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates, giving a bell-like sound.

clue.text: One-way ticket left out for char

indicators.note: an item left out is omitted, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: in Britain a one-way ticket is a single
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A one-way ticket is left out to be used by a cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like a British charwoman, a cleaner, but it is the verb to scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To char and to singe both mean to burn something lightly on the surface.

clue.text: Body of water, in a desert, he polluted

indicators.note: polluted water is fouled and disturbed, so these letters are mixed into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man fouls a pool of water out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, this sea is bordered by desert on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is the inlet of the Indian Ocean lying between Africa and Arabia.

clue.text: Place to meet briefly with sun goddess

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word drops its final letter

blocks.note: a venue is a place where people meet
S is an abbreviation for sun, as on weather maps

explanation.surface: A rendezvous spot for a quick meeting with a sun goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Artificial, some flowers at zoo

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters, a run inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: Some of the flowers at the zoo are fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior substitute or imitation, so made artificially rather than genuine.

clue.text: Fish - vet catching tons

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a vet is an animal surgeon
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: An animal doctor lands tons of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish whose roe is caviar.
